canonical_delta.bug: The browser terminal could emit binary xterm input immediately after WebSocket open while Clerk.session.getToken() was still awaiting. The server requires authentication to be the first text message, so sufficiently early user input could win the first-frame race and fail a legitimate session closed.
canonical_delta.initial_regression_issue: The first static source assertions used rendered single JavaScript braces, while terminal_gateway.py stores doubled braces inside the Python f-string source. Product code was unaffected; the test lineage was corrected rather than represented as green.
repair: Browser terminal input is disabled until the authenticated server ready frame is received.
Resize control messages are disabled until the authenticated server ready frame is received.
Binary terminal output is ignored until readiness is established.
An error or WebSocket close clears readiness again.
The server-side invariant that authentication must be the first message remains unchanged and fail-closed.

grf.observed: Client installed term.onData as soon as the socket existed; authentication token acquisition was asynchronous; server awaited receive_text() as its first message.
grf.hypothesis: Fast input before token acquisition can deliver a binary first frame and cause a legitimate authenticated terminal to be rejected.
grf.strongest_counterhypothesis: The browser/UI timing always prevents xterm input before the auth JSON is transmitted.
grf.falsifier: Show that pre-ready terminal input can never reach WebSocket.send, independent of UI timing.
grf.intervention: Introduce terminalReady=false and admit input/resize only after the server sends type=ready; clear it on error/close.
